back: A natural event that could cause loss of life, injury or damage to property and the environment.
A hazard event that seriously disrupts a community, causing losses it cannot cope with using its own resources.
How likely people and places are to suffer harm from a hazard (poverty, building quality, preparedness, access to help).
Primary: directly from the event (collapse, lava). Secondary: follow on (fires, disease, homelessness, job losses).
Fertile soils, geothermal energy, minerals, jobs in cities, tourism, attachment to place, poverty, confidence in protection.
Physical: magnitude, depth, distance, ground, secondary hazards. Human: population density, building quality, development, preparedness, time of day.
Haiti (LIC): magnitude 7.0, deaths estimated from about 100,000 to over 200,000. Canterbury, New Zealand (HIC): magnitude 7.1, no deaths directly from the shaking.
Soufrière Hills eruptions: 19 deaths in June 1997, capital Plymouth abandoned, southern exclusion zone, many people left the island.
